findings.summary: Message sending functions have inconsistent parameter ordering across implementations
evidence: SendTemplateMessage in messages.go uses OutgoingMessageRequest struct with embedded Account/Contact
Provider interface SendText/SendImage use (ctx, instanceID, to, content) parameter order
RevokeMessage has 3 different signatures across 5 files according to scan evidence
SendReaction has 3 different signatures across 5 files according to scan evidence
findings.suggestion: Standardize message sending API surface - either consolidate on provider.MessageProvider interface or create unified request/response types. The current mix of struct-based and positional parameters creates confusion.

findings.summary: Inconsistent response envelope patterns across handlers
evidence: Some handlers return r.SendEnvelope(map[string]interface{}{"accounts": response})
Others return r.SendEnvelope(map[string]any{"flows": response})
Inconsistent use of interface{} vs any for JSON payloads
Mixed error handling: some return nil after SendErrorEnvelope, others return the error
findings.suggestion: Create consistent response helper functions or standardize on one pattern. The variation makes the API surface harder to learn and use consistently.

findings.summary: Only 35 of 145 handlers use getOrgAndUserID, only 16 use requirePermission
evidence: 35 files use getOrgAndUserID pattern for auth extraction
Only 16 files use requirePermission for RBAC checks
516 total handler functions identified in codebase
Webhook handlers (WebhookVerify, WebhookHandler) skip auth checks (expected but undocumented)
Some handlers call HasPermission directly instead of using requirePermission helper
findings.suggestion: Audit all 516 handler functions and categorize: 1) Public routes (health, webhooks), 2) Authenticated routes missing RBAC, 3) Routes with proper auth. Create middleware or decorator pattern to enforce consistent authorization.

findings.summary: Contact assignment and chat access policies use manual permission checks
evidence: AssignContact uses HasPermission check inline instead of requirePermission helper
canViewRestrictedChatWithoutClaim and canSendRestrictedChatWithoutClaim implement custom auth logic
send restriction policies implement their own authorization bypass logic (canBypassPendingChatRestriction)
No centralized policy enforcement point - scattered across multiple files
findings.suggestion: Consolidate chat access and send restriction policies into a single authorization layer. Create a ChatAccessAuthorizer interface that consolidates all permission checks.

findings.summary: Multiple files exceed 1000 LOC with high complexity scores
evidence: chatbot_processor.go: 2912 LOC, complexity score 545
agent_transfers.go: 1465 LOC, complexity score 204
campaigns.go: 1409 LOC, complexity score 159
contacts.go: 1278 LOC, complexity score 177
chat_close_ratings.go: 1249 LOC, complexity score 170
findings.suggestion: Break down these mega-files into focused modules. For example, chatbot_processor.go could be split into: rule_engine.go, flow_executor.go, ai_context.go, session_manager.go. Aim for files under 500 LOC.

findings.summary: cache.go has 31 disconnected function clusters - mixed responsibilities
evidence: 31 functions in cache.go with 18 disconnected clusters per scan evidence
Caches chatbot settings, flows, keyword rules, WhatsApp accounts, webhooks, SLA settings, AI contexts, permissions, tags
No clear abstraction or interface - all functions are methods on App
Mixes cache logic with decryption logic (decryptChatbotAIKey)
754 LOC, untested (0 importers per scan evidence)
findings.suggestion: Extract a CacheManager interface with concrete implementation. Separate concerns: CacheManager (get/set/invalidate), CryptoHelper (decrypt/encrypt), and DomainCacheLayer (chatbot, permissions, etc.).

findings.summary: contacts_messaging.go has 7 disconnected function clusters (13 functions total)
evidence: 7 disconnected function clusters per scan evidence
861 LOC, complexity score 90
Functions span: message sending, media handling, revoking, reactions, typing indicators
Untested (0 importers per scan evidence)
findings.suggestion: Split into focused files: message_send.go, message_reactions.go, message_media.go, typing_indicators.go. Each should have a single clear responsibility.

findings.summary: Flow status uses deprecated marker but flows are still active
evidence: Line 277: 'Deprecated flows cannot be updated'
Line 455-457: 'Only PUBLISHED flows can be deprecated'
Line 479: Status set to 'DEPRECATED'
No evidence of deprecated flows being removed from database or API
3 deprecated markers found in codebase per migration signals
findings.suggestion: Either complete the migration by removing deprecated flows from queries/API, or remove the deprecated status if it's not being enforced. The current state is partial.

findings.summary: Provider abstraction exists but both Meta and Whatsmeow are actively used
evidence: MessageProvider interface defines 10 methods for abstraction
Both MetaAdapter and WhatsmeowAdapter implement the interface
No evidence one is being phased out - both appear actively maintained
Scan evidence shows consistent usage patterns across both implementations
findings.suggestion: This is actually good design - the abstraction allows multi-provider support. However, document which provider should be used for new features or if both should be maintained indefinitely.

findings.summary: High-complexity modules have zero test coverage
evidence: cache.go: 31 functions, 754 LOC, untested per scan evidence
contacts_management.go: 18 functions, 959 LOC, untested per scan evidence
import_export.go: 7 functions, 813 LOC, untested per scan evidence
message_persist.go: 674 LOC, untested per scan evidence
88 test files exist but don't cover these critical modules
Test coverage: 57 handlers, 88 test files (~50% coverage at file level)
findings.suggestion: Prioritize test coverage for these 5 modules immediately. They are critical paths (caching, messaging, data import) with zero coverage. Start with integration tests before unit tests.

findings.summary: Test files show evidence of implementation coupling
evidence: Tests import internal/handlers package directly
Tests likely depend on internal App structure and database setup
Multiple 1000+ line test files (campaigns_test.go: 1128 LOC, contacts_test.go: 1535 LOC)
Large test files suggest either: too many responsibilities in tested module, or brittle integration tests
findings.suggestion: Extract test utilities into test/testutil package (already exists). Break large test files into focused test suites. Add interface boundaries to reduce coupling to App internals.

findings.summary: No evidence of cross-module integration tests
evidence: Test files are co-located with source (handlers_test.go pattern)
Tests appear to be unit-level with database fixtures
No evidence of end-to-end workflow tests (e.g., campaign creation → execution → webhook handling)
Test fixtures in test/fixtures/models/factories.go (683 LOC) but unclear usage scope
findings.suggestion: Add integration test suite that covers critical workflows: 1) User auth → Permission check → Resource access, 2) Campaign launch → Message queue → Delivery, 3) Webhook receipt → Message processing → WebSocket broadcast.

findings.summary: Multiple files use config bag passing instead of structured parameters
evidence: Scan evidence shows 83 config bag mentions in cache.go
72 config bag mentions in messages.go
68 config bag mentions in pkg/whatsapp/client.go
OutgoingMessageRequest struct has 20+ fields mixing concerns (account, contact, template, media, reply context, flow data)
No clear abstraction boundaries - request struct does everything
findings.suggestion: Refactor OutgoingMessageRequest into focused request types: TextMessageRequest, MediaMessageRequest, TemplateMessageRequest, FlowMessageRequest. Use interface or builder pattern instead of god-object.

findings.summary: Super admin org switching logic embedded in getOrgID
evidence: getOrgID contains 40+ lines of org switching logic
Checks X-Organization-ID header
Validates super admin status
Queries database to verify org membership
No separate authorization layer - business logic mixed with context extraction
findings.suggestion: Extract org switching into authorizeOrgSwitch(orgID, userID, overrideOrgID) function. Add audit logging for org switches by super admins. The current inline logic is hard to test and audit.
